title: Performance Profiling & Benchmarking 📊
description: Measure latency, memory, and power with TFLite benchmark tools and Android Studio profiler.

slides.title: Don't Guess – Measure! ⏱️
slides.content:
# Why Profiling Matters

A model that takes 500ms per frame is useless for real‑time video. You need to know:
- **Inference latency** (min, max, average).
- **Memory consumption** (RAM and GPU memory).
- **Power usage** (battery drain).
- **Whether you are CPU‑bound or memory‑bound**.

TensorFlow Lite provides a **benchmark tool** and **profiling API**.

slides.title: TFLite Benchmark Tool (Command Line)
slides.content: Run on desktop or Android to get detailed timing.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Linux/macOS
tensorflow/lite/tools/benchmark/benchmark_model \
  --graph=model.tflite \
  --num_threads=4 \
  --warmup_runs=10 \
  --num_runs=50

# Android (via adb)
adb push model.tflite /data/local/tmp
adb shell /data/local/tmp/benchmark_model \
  --graph=/data/local/tmp/model.tflite \
  --use_gpu=true

quizData.question: Why include warmup runs in benchmarking?

options.text: To stabilise performance and avoid cold‑start overhead

quizData.explanation: Warmup runs allow the system to cache necessary resources, giving more representative steady‑state measurements.

slides.title: In‑App Profiling with TFLite Interpreter API 📊
slides.content:
# Programmatically Measure Latency

```kotlin
val start = SystemClock.uptimeMillis()
interpreter.run(input, output)
val end = SystemClock.uptimeMillis()
val latency = end - start
```

For a robust measurement, run multiple times and collect statistics.

Also use `Interpreter.Options().setUseXNNPACK(true)` for optimised CPU execution.

slides.title: Using Android Studio Profiler
slides.content:
Attach to running app and monitor CPU, memory, and energy. Look for:
- High CPU spikes during inference.
- Memory allocations per run.
- GPU utilisation if using GPU delegate.

slides.title: Use XNNPACK for CPU Boost 🚀
slides.content: XNNPACK is a highly optimised CPU backend. Enable it in the interpreter options. It's often the default in newer TFLite builds and can rival GPU delegates for small models.

slides.title: Benchmark Your Model 🛠️
slides.content: Take the MNIST model from the previous lesson, run the benchmark tool with CPU and GPU delegates, and compare the average latency. Share your findings!
